payload.brief: Produce a frozen Plan Package (plus decision record + handoff bundle) to build a new CouncilOS subsystem: an Implementation Council that consumes a frozen Planning Council output and produces a working implementation (repo changes + tests + build/release artifacts).
payload.problem_statement: CouncilOS currently lacks a deterministic, auditable, multi-agent subsystem for transforming frozen planning artifacts into working software implementations. The system must enforce separation of powers, maintain immutable audit trails, support long-horizon work across context-window limits via shared workspace, prevent silent scope expansion, use JSON-only artifacts with RFC 6901/6902 standards, and produce a complete freeze bundle suitable for handoff or checkpoint/resume.
goals: G1: Design end-to-end Implementation Council architecture conforming to all CouncilOS invariants (orchestrator authority, stochastic JSON-only workers, durable audit spine, single source of truth, no silent scope expansion)
G2: Define canonical input contract (plan_package_final.json, repo_context.json, workspace_context.json schemas)

G3: Define complete Implementation Freeze Bundle output contract with typed/versioned JSON artifacts (run_manifest, event_log, work_plan, patchsets, repo_snapshot, test_results, quality_reports, trace_report, review_findings, release_bundle, decision_record, workspace_index, context_packs, stage_handoffs)

G4: Design shared workspace system as versioned artifact extension supporting long-running work, canonical vs non-canonical separation, deterministic context packs, workspace governance, and resumable state handoff artifacts at every stage boundary
G5: Establish evidence+traceability standard using RFC 6901 JSON Pointer exclusively for all artifacts including repo state, code changes, and workspace state
G6: Define repair model using RFC 6902 JSON Patch for JSON artifacts and diff-only artifacts for code changes with deterministic orchestrator application

G7: Specify council structure with role separation (leader, implementer, integrator, reviewer, patcher, QA/release/devops, security/compliance, scribe/summarizer) ensuring writer/reviewer/judge separation and multi-vendor diversity

G8: Design staged workflow state machine (intake, work breakdown, parallel implementation pods, deterministic integration, tool-run validation loops, review+patch cycles, regression revalidation, stage handoff emission, freeze bundle production)
G9: Define tool permission matrix per stage, secrets policy with redaction/blocking, HITL triggers for high-risk operations, and deterministic enforcement rules
G10: Specify code-owned validators gating freeze (build/compile, lint/format/typecheck, tests+AT# execution, integrity, workspace integrity, risk closure, reproducibility/trace completeness)
G11: Design flaky/nondeterministic failure policy with retry budgets, quarantine/stabilization requirements, and escalation paths
G12: Define ChangeRequest artifact schema with deterministic rules for proposal, approval, and reroute to Planning Council when plan semantics must change
G13: Specify multi-vendor model portfolio with default routing for writers vs reviewers vs judges vs patchers
non_goals: NG1: Implementing the Implementation Council system itself (this project produces the plan only)
NG2: Modifying existing CouncilOS orchestrator code or Planning Council subsystems
NG3: Defining general-purpose CI/CD pipelines unrelated to CouncilOS multi-agent workflows
NG4: Supporting interactive development workflows or human-in-the-loop coding sessions
NG5: Creating new evidence pointer standards beyond RFC 6901 JSON Pointer
NG6: Designing workspace backends or storage infrastructure (only interface contracts and governance rules)
NG7: Implementing actual code generation, testing, or build tooling (only workflow/artifact design)

constraints.text: Orchestrator has sole authority over routing, budgets, iteration limits, termination, checkpoint/resume, tool permissions, selection logic, validator enforcement
LLM roles must output JSON-only artifacts matching per-stage schemas with no prose
Immutable run_manifest, append-only event_log, versioned artifact store required; checkpoint at every stage boundary
Downstream consumers use ONLY canonical artifacts, not chat logs
Implementation Council may not change semantics of R#/AT#/O#/K# from input plan without explicit ChangeRequest artifact + decision record + policy-triggered escalation
Evidence pointers MUST use RFC 6901 JSON Pointer objects referencing versioned JSON artifacts
JSON artifact repairs MUST use RFC 6902 JSON Patch arrays only
Code changes MUST use diff-only artifacts with deterministic orchestrator application + revalidation
Shared workspace must be versioned, auditable, checkpointed extension of artifact system, not informal scratchpad
Canonical vs non-canonical workspace content must be explicitly separated and marked
Secrets must never be stored in logs or workspace; detection + blocking required
Writer/reviewer/judge separation and multi-vendor diversity required in council structure
No silent scope expansion; large refactors must be decomposed into bounded patchsets + staged validation

assumptions.text: Planning Council output (plan_package_final.json) is well-formed, frozen, and contains complete R#/AT#/O#/K# specifications
Target repositories have deterministic build/test entrypoints and toolchain configurations that can be captured in repo_context.json
Workspace backend provides versioned file storage with atomic operations and sufficient capacity for long-running implementation work
Orchestrator can enforce forbidden-path rules and operation caps deterministically during patch application
Multi-vendor LLM APIs provide sufficient reliability and consistency for writer/reviewer/judge separation
Tool execution environment can be sandboxed with granular permission controls per stage
Test execution results can be deterministically mapped back to AT# acceptance test IDs from planning artifacts
Diff-based code change artifacts can be applied deterministically across potential merge conflicts and rebase scenarios
Context pack size bounds can be determined that balance completeness with LLM context window limits
Flaky test detection and quarantine can be automated with acceptable false positive/negative rates

open_questions.text: What is the maximum workspace size (GB) and retention period for non-canonical artifacts before compaction/summarization is required?
What specific diff format should be used for code change artifacts (unified diff, structured file-op diff, or other)?
How should the orchestrator deterministically select the smallest passing repair when multiple patch options are available?
What are the specific HITL trigger conditions and approval workflows for high-risk operations?
How should conflict resolution work when parallel implementation pods produce overlapping patchsets?
What is the retry budget and backoff strategy for flaky tests and nondeterministic tool failures?
How should the system handle dependencies that require network access or package manager operations during implementation?
What are the specific criteria for when a ChangeRequest must be escalated vs handled within Implementation Council?
How should the system handle incremental implementation when the full work plan cannot be completed within token/time budgets?
What is the schema for repo_context.json protected paths and how are they enforced during patch application?
How should context packs be bounded and selected when workspace state grows beyond context window limits?
What specific security/compliance checks are required in quality_reports.json and how are they executed?

success_metrics: SM1: Complete Implementation Freeze Bundle schema definitions with all required artifacts specified (run_manifest, event_log, work_plan, patchsets, repo_snapshot, test_results, quality_reports, trace_report, review_findings, release_bundle, decision_record, workspace_index, context_packs, stage_handoffs) - target: 100% coverage

SM2: All CouncilOS invariants explicitly addressed in architecture (separation of powers, JSON-only outputs, durable audit spine, single source of truth, no silent scope expansion) - target: 5/5 invariants enforced

SM3: Shared workspace design includes all required elements (versioning, auditability, checkpointing, canonical/non-canonical separation, context packs, governance, state handoff artifacts) - target: 7/7 elements specified
SM4: Evidence+traceability uses RFC 6901 JSON Pointer exclusively with no alternative pointer standards - target: 100% compliance
SM5: Repair model uses RFC 6902 JSON Patch for JSON and diff-only for code with deterministic application rules - target: 100% compliance
SM6: Council structure specifies all required roles with writer/reviewer/judge separation - target: minimum 7 roles with clear separation
SM7: Workflow state machine covers all required stages from intake through freeze bundle production - target: minimum 9 stages with checkpoint boundaries
SM8: Tool permission matrix defined per stage with secrets policy and HITL triggers - target: complete matrix for all stages
SM9: Code-owned validators specified for all freeze gates (build, lint, tests, integrity, workspace integrity, risk closure, trace completeness) - target: minimum 7 validators
SM10: Flaky failure policy includes retry budgets, quarantine requirements, and escalation paths - target: all 3 elements specified
SM11: ChangeRequest artifact schema with deterministic proposal/approval/reroute rules - target: complete schema + rules
SM12: Multi-vendor model portfolio with routing for writers/reviewers/judges/patchers - target: minimum 4 role types with vendor diversity
stakeholders: Artifact schema and validation framework maintainers
End users requiring deterministic software implementation workflows

glossary.definition: Normalized intake artifact capturing problem statement, goals, constraints, assumptions, open questions, success metrics, and stakeholders for a CouncilOS project
CouncilOS subsystem that consumes frozen Planning Council output and produces working implementation with repo changes, tests, and build/release artifacts
Upstream CouncilOS subsystem that produces frozen plan_package_final.json with requirements (R#), acceptance tests (AT#), objectives (O#), and key results (K#)
Deterministic code component with sole authority over routing, budgets, iteration limits, termination, checkpoint/resume, tool permissions, selection logic, and validator enforcement
CouncilOS invariant ensuring orchestrator controls workflow while LLM roles are stochastic workers producing only JSON artifacts
Immutable run_manifest, append-only event_log, and versioned artifact store with checkpoints at every stage boundary
CouncilOS invariant requiring downstream consumers use only canonical artifacts, not chat logs or ephemeral state
Forbidden practice where agents change semantics of requirements/tests/objectives without explicit ChangeRequest artifact and approval
Versioned, auditable, tool-accessible storage system for persisting progress across context-window limits and coordinating multi-agent work
Typed, versioned JSON artifact used by validators and downstream councils as authoritative source
Optional working notes or summaries that are stored and versioned but explicitly marked as non-authoritative
Bounded, deterministically-compiled subset of workspace artifacts provided to agents at each stage, with explicit selection rules
RFC 6901 JSON Pointer object referencing versioned JSON artifact: {artifact_ref, entity_id|null, json_pointer, note}
Standard for identifying specific values within JSON documents using path strings starting with /
Standard for expressing modifications to JSON documents as arrays of operations (add, remove, replace, move, copy, test)
JSON artifact embedding code diffs with deterministic apply order for repo modifications
JSON artifact capturing resumable state at checkpoint boundary: current objectives, completed tasks, pending blockers, next actions, and pointers into work artifacts

Complete set of canonical output artifacts from Implementation Council including run_manifest, event_log, work_plan, patchsets, test_results, quality_reports, trace_report, review_findings, release_bundle, decision_record, workspace_index, context_packs, and stage_handoffs
Code-owned deterministic function that gates stage transitions or freeze by checking artifact integrity, completeness, and quality criteria
Explicit artifact proposing deviation from frozen plan semantics, requiring approval and potentially triggering reroute to Planning Council
CouncilOS pattern ensuring agents that produce artifacts are distinct from those that review them and those that make approval decisions
Practice of using different LLM providers for writers vs reviewers vs judges to reduce correlated failures and bias
Repository path or workspace namespace that agents are not permitted to modify, enforced by orchestrator during patch application
Test that exhibits nondeterministic pass/fail behavior requiring retry budgets, quarantine, or stabilization
Human-In-The-Loop: policy-triggered escalation requiring human approval for high-risk operations
Code-enforced logic for bounded retries with backoff, distinct from agent-controlled iteration
Dense artifact mapping requirements (R#) to tasks to patchsets/commits to files/modules to tests to acceptance test (AT#) results
JSON artifact describing existing codebase: locator/path, base commit SHA, build/test entrypoints, toolchain constraints, dependency/network policy, protected paths, secrets handling
JSON artifact describing shared workspace backend: file store location, size limits, allowed formats, retention policy, namespaces, access control
Canonical JSON artifact indexing all workspace items with types, versions, provenance, and pointers
Structured artifact capturing lint, typecheck, security scan, dependency check, and license compliance results
Artifact manifest listing build outputs, package metadata, container digests, and other deployment artifacts
Artifact documenting why key implementation decisions were made and what conditions would change them
Optional agent role producing non-canonical summaries and context packs without authority to modify canonical artifacts
